NL-FOL: natural language to first-order logic translation (autoformalization)
autoformalization: automatic translation of informal (natural language) statements into formal logic
faithfulness: whether a candidate FOL formula correctly captures the meaning of its source sentence
gold formula: a human-written reference FOL formula for a sentence
gold-free: requiring no human-written reference formula at evaluation time
FOLIO: a dataset of FOL-annotated natural language inference problems (Han et al. 2022)
MALLS: a dataset of NL-FOL pairs generated and verified with GPT-4 (Yang et al. 2023)
Logic-LM: a neuro-symbolic framework prompting LLMs for FOL and calling a prover (Pan et al. 2023)
z3: the Z3 SMT solver used for logical equivalence and satisfiability checks
AUROC: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
DeLong test: a nonparametric test comparing two correlated AUROCs on the same sample
track L: the LLM-output evaluation track: candidate formulas produced by LLM systems
track H: the human-annotation evaluation track: original gold formulas from dataset annotators
FOL-Triage: the proposed three-layer gold-free faithfulness checker (L1 lint, L2 accounting, L3 questionnaire)
L1 (Formula Lint): text-free deterministic checks for formula smells (e.g. existential implication, free variables, vacuity)
L2 (Text Accounting): bag-of-words and role-aware content coverage checks comparing text to formula, no LLM
L3 (Role Questionnaire): a small LLM reads the text only and z3 reads the formula only; their structured answers are compared
c_score: cross-system consensus score: 1 minus the fraction of peer systems whose formula is z3-equivalent to the candidate
eq_frac: the fraction of peer translations z3-equivalent to the candidate formula
medoid: the peer formula that is z3-equivalent to the largest cluster of translations
medoid depth: the number of typed repair steps from a candidate to the consensus medoid
cluster entropy: Shannon entropy of the z3-equivalence class sizes among peer translations
self-consistency: sampling K translations from the same model and measuring agreement (SC-K)
SC-5: self-consistency with K=5 samples from the same or a cheap model
peer pool: the set of independent translations of the same sentence by different LLM families
typed repair: a minimal edit from one FOL formula to another, classified by operator type
NEG: repair operator: polarity or negation error
QUANT: repair operator: wrong quantifier (universal vs existential)
RESTR: repair operator: missing or wrong restrictor in a quantified expression
MOVE: repair operator: scope or attachment error
DROP: repair operator: a predicate or condition present in the text is missing from the formula
ADD: repair operator: a predicate or condition absent from the text appears in the formula
SWAP: repair operator: arguments of a predicate are in the wrong order
BIND: repair operator: a variable binding error (e.g. free variable, wrong quantifier scope)
SCOPE: repair operator: incorrect quantifier or connective scope
UNGLUE: repair operator: two concepts incorrectly merged into one predicate
COMPOUND: a formula error requiring more than one typed repair operator to fix
vocabulary alignment: matching predicate and constant names between two formulas that may use different naming conventions
ADD+DROP: a pair of repair operators often indicating a vocabulary mismatch rather than a semantic error
subst_only: an error consisting solely of ADD+DROP, i.e. likely a vocabulary difference not a semantic mistake
meaning-preserving rewrite: a transformation of a formula that does not change its truth conditions (e.g. renaming, reordering, De Morgan, contrapositive)
RENAME: meaning-preserving rewrite: systematic renaming of predicates or constants
REORDER: meaning-preserving rewrite: reordering conjuncts or disjuncts
DEMORGAN: meaning-preserving rewrite: applying De Morgan's law
CONTRAPOSITIVE: meaning-preserving rewrite: replacing an implication with its contrapositive
false alarm rate: the fraction of correct items incorrectly flagged as errors (false positive rate on correct items)
flip rate: the fraction of items whose binary verdict changes after a meaning-preserving rewrite
coverage: the fraction of items for which a metric produces a score (unparseable items counted)
disguised: sentences with content words replaced by nonce words, used to test for memorisation of public benchmarks
nonce words: nonsense words substituted for content words to break surface-level memorisation
contamination: the risk that an LLM-based metric has memorised the gold formulas of a public benchmark
difference-in-differences (DiD): comparing the disguise effect on track H (memorisable) vs track L (not memorisable) to detect contamination
round-trip verification: verbalising a formula back to natural language and comparing to the original sentence
NLI: natural language inference: classifying whether one sentence entails, contradicts, or is neutral to another
decomposed judge: an ablation where the LLM reads the formula directly instead of z3 answering the schema
cross-fitted: training and predicting on non-overlapping folds to avoid overfitting
prevalence: the base rate of errors in the evaluation set
panel adjudication: having multiple independent judges vote on each label, with majority or unanimity rules
fused score: a logistic combination of multiple layer scores, fitted on track H and applied to track L
formula smell: a syntactic pattern in FOL that is valid but almost always indicates a semantic error
existential implication: the pattern exists x (A(x) -> B(x)), which is vacuously true if any x fails A
vacuity: a formula or subformula that is trivially satisfied regardless of the interpretation
bag-of-words: a text representation ignoring word order, counting only word occurrences
role-aware check: comparing the semantic roles (subject, object, modifier) of text content words to formula predicates
UD: Universal Dependencies: a framework for consistent cross-linguistic grammatical annotation
Udep2Mono: a tool that computes monotonicity profiles from Universal Dependencies parses (Chen & Gao 2021)
monotonicity: whether a position in a logical expression preserves or reverses entailment (upward or downward)
Smatch: a metric for comparing semantic graphs by finding a maximum common subgraph
FRANK: a benchmark and typology for factuality errors in abstractive summarisation (Pagnoni et al. 2021)
QuestEval: a QA-based factuality metric that generates and answers questions (Scialom et al. 2021)
CLOVER: a metric using counter-interpretations and LLM oracles for logical validity (Ryu et al. 2024)
StrongReject: a benchmark for evaluating refusal in safety-aligned LLMs
SyGNS: a dataset of syntactic generalisation in NLI with monotonicity annotations (Yanaka et al. 2021)
Brunello et al. 2025: study showing LLMs achieve 72-100% equivalence to gold FOL on curated benchmarks
Brunello et al. 2026: audit finding ~42% error rates in FOLIO and MALLS gold annotations
Thatikonda et al. 2025: evaluation of FOL closeness metrics under controlled perturbations
ccg2lambda: a symbolic NL-FOL system using CCG parsing and lambda calculus
flash-lite: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, the primary cheap LLM used for L3 and judging
gpt-4.1-nano: OpenAI GPT-4.1 Nano, used as a cheap secondary judge (logprob-based)
gemini-3.1-pro: Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, used as a strong/frontier judge
sentence-cluster bootstrap: a bootstrap procedure clustering by sentence to respect non-independence of items from the same sentence
Wilson interval: a confidence interval for a binomial proportion with better coverage than the Wald interval
strong judge: a large frontier LLM (e.g. Gemini 3.1 Pro) used as an expensive but more accurate judge
cheap judge: a small or flash-tier LLM used as a fast, inexpensive judge baseline
cross-system equivalence: checking whether translations by different LLM families are logically equivalent via z3
frontier model: the largest and most capable commercially available LLM at the time of evaluation
meta-evaluation: evaluating a metric's ability to predict the correctness of NL-FOL translations
item-level AUROC: AUROC computed at the level of individual (sentence, formula) pairs
system-level correlation: correlation between a metric's aggregate score and a system's true error rate
complexity stratum: a subset of items grouped by sentence complexity (length, quantifier count, nesting depth)
exception sentence: a sentence containing exception clauses (e.g. 'unless', 'except') that are hard to formalise
